articles.title: Israel kills three in airstrike on Jenin
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: The Israeli Army announced on Friday, August 28 that it launched a drone strike in the northern West Bank city of Jenin, killing three Palestinian resistance fighters. It added that Qais Bitawi, whom it described as a Hamas operative in the dismantled Jenin Brigade, was among the fatalities. The other two slain men were identified as Basel Turkman and Ahmad Yaqoub Turkman, according to local media outlets which also reported that the bodies of the three Palestinians were confiscated by the Israeli forces. The deadly attack marks the first Israeli airstrike in the occupied West Bank in 10 months. articles.author: Rania Khalek
articles.content_excerpt: “The commodification of child imprisonment” under Donald Trump is making CoreCivic and GEO Group executives even richer, Rep. articles.title: China saw this coming: Why Trump’s Iran sanctions won’t work with Dr. Ken Hammond
articles.author: Rania Khalek
articles.content_excerpt: Beijing just proved the limits of Washington’s sanctions machine. As US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent rolls out “Operation Economic Outcast,” China is doing what almost no other country in the world can: refusing to comply with US sanctions on Iran. Dr. Ken Hammond, professor of East Asian and Global History at New Mexico State University, joins Rania Khalek and Zoe Alexandra to unpack how Trump’s promised “economic D-Day” is running headfirst into a wall, as Beijing shields Chinese companies from “illegitimate” US sanctions and continues to buy up to 90% of Iran’s sanctioned crude oil exports. source_folders: 06_左派ニュース・社会主義戦略

articles.title: Right-wing attack on university in West Bengal sparks mass protests
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: Massive protests were organized in cities and towns across the Indian state of West Bengal on Wednesday, August 26 protesting against the rising right-wing attacks on the educational institutions and activists. This was the third such protest action taken since the August 20 midnight attack on the university by the ultra right-wing and Hindu supremacist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)-affiliated student organization Akhil Bhartiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP). Several students and teachers were injured in the attack and university property was vandalized. Students have lodged accusations that the security forces were unresponsive, while elected members of the state legislative assembly from the ruling BJP were directly involved. articles.title: Military government in Guinea-Bissau seeks to reshape political system with referendum
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Guinea-Bissau is set to vote on a new constitution on Sunday, August 30, in a referendum that could alter the country’s political system and strengthen the powers of the presidency. The referendum comes nine months after the military seized control. The crisis traces back to November 23, 2025, when Guinea-Bissau held presidential and parliamentary elections. Both incumbent President Umaro Sissoco Embaló and opposition candidate Fernando Dias da Costa claimed victory. Before the electoral commission could release provisional results, the military intervened on November 26, one day ahead of the announcement suspending the vote count and arresting opposition figures including PAIGC leader Domingos Simões Pereira and PRS’s Francisco da Costa. articles.title: Health activists in India demand affordable breast cancer treatments
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Health activists and public health experts in India are pushing for affordable breast cancer treatments as the Kerala High Court continues to hear a case originally filed in 2022. The case and the surrounding advocacy concern access to the medications ribociclib and abemaciclib – both of which have demonstrated significant benefits for patients with early-stage breast cancer but remain prohibitively expensive for a large part of the population. Breast cancer represents a true public health crisis in India, noted the Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatment. In 2024 , of the 780,000 new cancer cases among women, breast cancer accounted for 237,000 diagnoses.
